senses.definition: Meeting the standards, requirements, and training for a position.
Restricted or limited by conditions.
examples: Assuming that I have all the information, my qualified opinion is that your plan will work.

senses.definition: To describe or characterize something by listing its qualities.
To successfully fall under some category or description by meeting requisite conditions.
To make someone competent or eligible for some position or task.
To become competent or eligible for some position or task.
The kind, condition, and/or the set of characteristics of something, as opposed to the quantity of something.
examples: The lattice structure of a steel profoundly changes its qualities.

senses.definition: A single trait.
examples: While being impulsive can be great for artists, it is not a desirable quality for engineers.
Security, stability, and efficiency are good qualities of an operating system.

senses.definition: Good characteristics in particular; level of excellence; freedom of faults and flaws.
examples: This school is well-known for having teachers of high quality.
Quality of life is usually determined by health, education, and income.
He called for China’s cooperation in efforts to improve air quality.

senses.definition: Good worth, good make.
examples: For this building project we need to use quality materials that will last for many decades.
That was a quality game by Jim Smith.
We had some quality time yesterday!

senses.definition: A fundamental, generic term used when referring to the measurement (count, amount) of a scalar, vector, number of items or to some other way of denominating the value of a collection or group of items.
examples: You have to choose between quantity and quality.

senses.definition: An indefinite amount of something.
examples: Some soap making oils are best as base oils, used in a larger quantity in the soap, while other oils are best added in a small quantity.
Olive oil can be used practically in any quantity.

senses.definition: A specific measured amount.
examples: This bag would normally cost $497.50 for a quantity of 250, at a price of $1.99 per piece.
Generally it should not be used in a quantity larger than 15 percent.

senses.definition: A considerable measure or amount.
examples: The Boeing P-26A was the first all-metal monoplane fighter produced in quantity for the U.S. Army Air Corps.

senses.definition: The total amount of something; quantity.
The amount of compensation awarded to a successful party in a lawsuit.
The length or magnitude of the sentence handed down to someone who has been found guilty of a crime.
The amount or quantity observably present, or available.
Each of four equal parts into which something can be divided; a fourth part.
examples: I ate a quarter of the pizza.

senses.definition: A fourth part of a pound; approximately 113 grams.
A fourth part of the year; 3 months; a term or season.
A fourth part of an hour; a period of fifteen minutes, especially with reference to the quarter before or after the hour.
Housing, barracks, or other habitation or living space.
The place where someone or something lives.
A commonly played university drinking game in North America.
Quarterfinals.
The wife, consort, or widow of a king.
examples: The divorced king was looking for a new queen.

senses.definition: A female monarch.
The Virgin Mary (especially in formulations such as Queen of Heaven, Queen of Glory).
An excellent woman.
A journey or effort in pursuit of a goal (often lengthy, ambitious, or fervent); a mission.
examples: The hero's quest.

senses.definition: A task that a player may complete in order to gain a reward or advance the story.
The act of seeking, or looking after anything; attempt to find or obtain; search; pursuit.
examples: To rove in quest of game, of a lost child, of property, etc.

senses.definition: To seek or pursue a goal; to undertake a mission or job.
A worded or expressed sentence, phrase, or only a word on its own, which asks for information, a reply, or a response; an interrogative.
examples: What is your question?

senses.definition: A subject or topic for consideration or investigation.
examples: The question of seniority will be discussed at the meeting.
There was a question of which material to use.
I've ordered it all, but there’s still the question of who’s going to pay.

senses.definition: A doubt or challenge about the truth, accuracy, or validity of a matter.
examples: His claim to the property has come under question.
The story is true beyond question.
He obeyed without question.

senses.definition: A proposal to a meeting as a topic for deliberation.
examples: I move that the question be put to a vote.

senses.definition: The action of asking questions; a survey; an inquiry.
The act of challenging, wondering, and doubting.
Interrogation.
Characterized by questions, inquisitiveness, doubt, or wonder; quizzical.
examples: Why do you have a questioning look? Are you puzzled about something?

senses.definition: A game in which players must only say questions, and if they don't they lose.
Moving with speed, rapidity or swiftness, or capable of doing so; rapid; fast.
examples: I ran to the station – but I wasn't quick enough.
He's a quick runner.

senses.definition: Occurring in a short time; happening or done rapidly.
examples: That was a quick meal.

senses.definition: Lively, fast-thinking, witty, intelligent.
examples: You have to be very quick to be able to compete in ad-lib theatrics.

senses.definition: Mentally agile, alert, perceptive.
examples: My father is old but he still has a quick wit.

senses.definition: Rapidly; with speed; fast; with expedition.
examples: Luckily, the error was quickly corrected.

senses.definition: Very soon.
examples: If we go this way, we'll get there quickly.

senses.definition: Making little or no noise.
examples: The engine is remarkably quiet at low speed.
Please be quiet during the examination.

senses.definition: Without much activity, excitement, or disturbance.
examples: We had a quiet weekend at home.
It is a quiet street, apart from the school run.

senses.definition: Producing little or no noise.
Without attracting attention.
Released from obligation, penalty, etc; free, clear, or rid.
To leave (a place).
examples: The British quit India in the 1940s.

senses.definition: To set at rest; to free, as from anything harmful or oppressive; to relieve; to clear; to liberate.
To release from obligation, accusation, penalty, etc.; to absolve; to acquit.
With verbs, especially past participles.
With prepositional phrases and spatial adverbs.
With predicative adjectives.
With attributive adjectives, following an (especially indefinite) article; chiefly as expressing contrast, difference etc.
A statement attributed to a person; a quotation.
examples: She loved reading quotes of famous people.

senses.definition: A quotation mark.
A summary of work to be done with a set price; a quotation.
examples: After going over the hefty quotes, the board decided it was cheaper to have the project executed by its own staff.

senses.definition: A price set and offered (by the potential seller) for a financial security or commodity; a quotation.
